checks.label: If a number is multiplied by −1, its arrow is turned through 180 degrees: each × −1 turns the arrow 180°, from 1 to −1 and on round to 1, and half way it points straight up at full length, a turn and never a flip through 0
Multiplying by j corresponds to a rotation by +90 degrees: each × j turns the arrow 90° anticlockwise, round 1, j, −1, −j and back to 1, landing each time on the product
j² = −1: two quarter turns land the arrow from 1 on −1, and two turns of 270° (−j × −j) land there too

Known answers worked by hand: 3 × 3 = 9 and −3 × −3 = 9; (j3)² = −9 and (−j3)² = −9; j2 × j3 = −6; j³ = −j, j⁴ = 1, j⁵ = j; 45° twice is 90°, 270° twice is 540°; (j4)² = −16; (j2)² + 4 = 0, 2² + 4 = 8, (j4)² + 4 = −12
From outside the formula: putting the page's roots −1 + j2 and −1 − j2 back into x² + 2x + 5 gives 0, and the worked example −3 ± j2 makes x² + 6x + 13 zero

Every turn and stretch lands where multiplying says: on every screen and for every answer the arrow ends on the product of its factors, x itself is the stop on the way, and the working shows that product

Each puzzle takes only its right answer, and each wrong answer lands somewhere else: no number on the line squares to −9; of 45°, 90° and 180° only 90° done twice lands on −1; j³ = −j; only ±j3 square to −9; j3 × j2 = −6; j⁵ = j; ±j2 solve x² + 4 = 0
Of every turn the handle can set, 5° apart, only a quarter turn (90°) and three quarters (270°) land on −1 when done twice, and the dashed arrow is always at twice the turn
Before an answer, a puzzle's picture shows only the question: the arrow still on 1 and one line of working

Every demonstration finishes within 4.6 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.6 s; each tap of × −1 or × j within 1.6 s
